Zamboanga del Norte Dear Ms. Calasang: Thts has reference to your Letter dated November 6, 2024. concerntng the Dec.lsjon of the Court of Appeals (CA), Manila 5th Division in CA-G R SP No 156567_ dated July As represented, in 2018 you were severed from service as Supply Offcer IV of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of Dapitan, Zamboanga del Norte. followng the Ombudsman's decision finding you guilty of grave misconduct Wth a penalty of dtsmissal from service. It is intimated that since then, you have been depnved of salary and all benefits you are entitled to receive due to your termination from servce. The CA, in the aforementioned Decision, partially granted your petition and subsequently modified the decision of the Ombudsman in OMB-C-A-IS-OI IS from guilty of Grave Misconduct to only Simple Misconduct; and from a penalty of Dtsmssai from Service to a Penalty of Suspension of three (3) months. You submitted that in light of the decision of the CA downgrading the offense. you are entitled to reinstatement to your position and that you should be paid back wages. which will cover the monthly salary and monetary benefits you are entitled to receive from the date you were dismissed until your reinstatement in your post You made reference to Ombudsman Administrative Order (AO) No. 7. as amended by AO No. 17, Rule Ill, Section 7, which provides: "Section 7. Finality and execution of decision. Xxx An appeal shall not stop the decision from being executory. In case the penalty is suspension or removal and the respondent wins such appeal, he shall be considered as having been under preventive suspension and shall be paid the salary and such other emoluments that he did not receive by reason of tie suspension or removal." Hence. your subject request. mile this Department submits that your request for reinstatement in your previous post is tenable following the CA Decision, we cannot concur with your view that you are entitled to back wages. Here, it bears noting that the law governing the propriety for back wages or back salaries of public officers and employees is embodied under "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Rule 14 (Payment of Back Wages and Other Similar Benefits) of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Resolution 17010771. Section 74 thereof provides, thus: "The following are entitled to back wages and other similar benefits: a. An illegally dismissed or suspended official or employee who is exonerated/reprimanded and ordered reinstated in the service; and b. A respondent placed under preventive suspension, whose order Of suspension was declared by the Commission as invalid." Corollarily, Section 7 of Ombudsman AO, as above-cited, is unambiguous. It explicitly provides that "in case the penalty is suspension or removal and the respondent wins such appeal. he shall be considered as having been under preventive suspension and shall be paid the salary and such other emoluments that he did not receive by reason of the suspension or removal. " (Emphasis ours) Jurisprudence-wise, the Supreme Court has consistently equated the phrase "in the event he wins the appeal" with exoneration of the offence charged.2 It is quite clear that the element of exoneration of the offense charged is a condition sine qua non before one may be entitled back wages. Ergo, back wages shall be paid only if the government official or employee is completely exonerated of •the charge against him and his dismissal is found and declared to be unjustified. Stated differently, the concerned government official or employee must not be found guilty (even the slightest wrongdoing) of the offense charged. Accordingly, while the Court of Appeals ultimately found you liable for only Simple Misconduct, which is punishable by three (3) months suspension, the fact remains the same that you were not fully exonerated of the offense charged. To bolster this, in Jacinto v. CA,3 the Supreme Court upheld that: "However, in Balingasan, finding that petitioners therein indeed participated in the unlawful mass actions for which they were similarly meted suspension, the Court opined that they were not completely exonerated of the charges against them. They were denied back salaries because they had given ground for their suspension. This means that being found liable for a lesser offense is not equivalent to exoneration from the original complaint against the concerned public officer or employee. Balingasan referred to the earlier case of Yacia vs. City of Baguio, in which this Court denied the claim of an employee for backwages for the period during which he was not allowed to work because of the execution of the CSC decision dismissing him for Dishonesty, even though, on appeal, his penalty was reduced to a fine equivalent to six month's pay. Based on the above premises, petitioners' demand for backwages cannot be granted, for they had given cause for their suspension — their unjustified abandonment of classes to the prejudice of their students. 2017 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service (2017 RACCS), promulgated on July 3, 2017. 2 See Miranda v. Commission on Audit. G.R. NO. 84613, August 16. 1991. 200 SCRA 657; Abellera vs. City of Baguio, et al., G.R. NO. L-23957, March 18, 1967, 125 SCRA 1033: ranala vs. Legaspi, et al.. G.R. No. L-22537. March 31, 1965, 13 SCRA 566. 3 281 SCRA 657 Page 2 of 2

Although they were eventually found guilty only of conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service, and not grave misconduct or other offense warranting their dismissal from the service, they were not fully innocent of the charges against them." premised from the foregoing, this Department opines that your claim for back wages is untenable. Notwithstanding, please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: 10—3 ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jam Cc: PAISAL O.
